reason: The pitch names my actual problem, fewer bad requests and less chasing after documents, and I like being an early client, but I am being asked to be one of the first two for a founder who does this on the side, 10 hours a week, with no consultant who has run it through a real call for proposals. 4,080 EUR in the first year is over four percent of my firm's revenue; I will not sign a 12-month contract on a promise I cannot check.
objection: The AI eligibility pre-check is the part I would pay for, and it is the part I trust least: PNRR, AFIR and the regional programmes change their conditions every few months, and I have not seen who keeps the rules current. If it marks a farmer ineligible with a confident reason and he goes to the competitor down the street, that automation has cost me a client. And when something breaks the week before a submission deadline, one working day from a part-time founder is too slow.
would_change_my_mind: Let me feed the eligibility check my last 20 real requests and show me it gets at least the obvious ones right, or give me the phone number of one Romanian grant consultant who has used the document portal through a full submission round. Either of those and I would take the launch price.
